Private money is now backing Gulf robotics: Uber's $50m for Dubai robotaxis, a humanoid-robot ETF on ADX, and Oman's sovereign fund in a $200m round.

This week's 5 verified signals (15 to 19 Nov):
▸ UAE: Uber commits $50m over two years to take driverless rides door to door in Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim, then Downtown, DIFC and Business Bay
▸ UAE: Lunate's Boreas VettaFi Humanoid Robots ETF (ticker ROBOTS) is due to list on ADX on 8 Dec, holding 41 companies at a 0.49% fee
▸ UAE: Keeta Drone's M-Drone 4L lowers orders of up to 4.5 kg on a winch, for villa communities like Sobha Hartland
▸ UAE: Sheikh Shakhbout Medical City passes 1,300 robot-assisted surgeries, now 500+ a year
▸ Oman: the Oman Investment Authority joins a ~$200m round for Chinese lab-robot maker MegaRobo

Swipe for the detail. Sources in the comments.

#Robotics #UAE #Oman #AutonomousVehicles #Humanoids

posts.text:
Big 5 Global opens in Dubai today, so we're looking back at the region's biggest 3D-printing project.

In June 2025, UCC Holding and Qatar's Public Works Authority (Ashghal) started printing two public schools in Doha, 20,000 m² each, on COBOD BOD XL gantry printers. UCC called it the world's largest 3D-printed construction project.

▸ Printed at night, to avoid the heat
▸ Two schools in a 14-school package
▸ Where it stands: COBOD's project page, updated in June 2026, says the first school is underway. We haven't seen a completion announcement yet.

Seventeen months on: is it still the largest 3D-printed project in the world, or has something overtaken it in 2026? Tell us in the comments.

#Robotics #Construction #Qatar #3DPrinting #Big5Global

posts.text:
Who drives a container crane at Jeddah's port? Increasingly, an operator at a control station.

DP World has spent the year automating its South Container Terminal, one piece at a time:

▸ Oct 2026: 17 automated electric yard cranes (RTGs), a $56m investment, so 50 of the 77 are now electric and automated
▸ Jul 2026: 35 electric terminal tractors
▸ Mar 2026: three semi-automated quay cranes
▸ By 2030: the target is 100% electric equipment

The result so far: more than 221,200 containers (TEU) in July 2026, the terminal's busiest month since 1999.

It's one of 17 Saudi deployments in our database. Sources and the record are in the comments. Which Gulf port automates its yard next?

#Robotics #Ports #SaudiArabia #Logistics #Automation

This week's roundup. I run roboticsmena.com, the database these come from, and every item has a source you can check.

UAE: Uber says it will spend $50m over two years to expand driverless rides in Dubai: door to door in Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim, then Downtown, DIFC and Business Bay by the end of 2027, with a safety specialist on board at first.
Source: The National, https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/uae/2026/11/18/uber-commits-50m-to-expand-autonomous-vehicle-services-across-dubai-by-2027/

UAE: Lunate's Boreas VettaFi Humanoid Robots ETF (ticker ROBOTS) is due to list on the Abu Dhabi exchange on 8 Dec. It starts with 41 companies across chips, parts, robot makers and software, at 0.49% a year.
Source: Lunate, https://lunate.com/en/news-insights/announcements/lunate-expands-boreas-range-with-launch-of-gccs-first-humanoid-robots-etf/

UAE: Keeta Drone showed the M-Drone 4L at Dubai Future Week. It hovers and lowers orders of up to 4.5 kg on a cable, so it needs no landing pad. Sobha Hartland is expected to be one of the first communities. No start date yet.
Source: Keeta Drone press release on Zawya, https://www.zawya.com/en/press-release/events-conferences/keeta-drone-unveils-its-latest-delivery-solutions-at-dubai-future-week-2348805

UAE: Sheikh Shakhbout Medical City in Abu Dhabi has passed 1,300 robot-assisted surgeries and now does more than 500 a year.
Source: Gulf News, https://gulfnews.com/uae/health/sheikh-shakhbout-medical-city-performs-1300-robotic-assisted-surgeries-1.500748148

Oman: the Oman Investment Authority joined a round of nearly $200m for MegaRobo, a Chinese maker of robotic lab systems. Nothing has been announced about operations in Oman.
Source: The AI Insider, https://theaiinsider.tech/2026/11/19/megarobo-raises-nearly-200m-to-fund-expansion-of-ai-powered-laboratory-automation/

Big 5 Global (the construction show) is at Dubai World Trade Centre from 23 to 26 Nov. If you go and see robots on the floor, post them here.

What did we miss in your country this week?

posts.title: [Data] Construction robots in MENA: 10 verified deployments, and half of them are in Saudi Arabia
posts.text:
With Big 5 on in Dubai this week I pulled every construction record from our database (roboticsmena.com, which I run). 10 of the 70 deployments we've verified so far are construction. Here they are, with what's actually on a site and what's still a plan.

Saudi Arabia (5)
NEOM and Samsung C&T: a rebar-cage automation joint venture, initial investment of more than SAR 1.3bn (Dec 2024). The robots weld and tie pre-manufactured cages.
Source: Asharq Al-Awsat, https://english.aawsat.com/business/5093451-neom-samsung-ct-commit-worlds-largest-deployment-rebar-construction-automation
Jeddah: a 5,600 m² mosque printed with four Guanli printers. Reports say the printing covered non-structural parts.
Source: Gulf Construction Online, https://www.gulfconstructiononline.com/Article/386820/Jeddah_hosts_world%E2%80%99s_first_3D_printed_mosque
Also: Riyadh Municipality's robots and drones for drains and bridges, a Roads General Authority culvert-inspection robot, and AM Unique adding Black Buffalo 3D concrete printers.

UAE (4)
A 3D concrete printing factory in KEZAD, Abu Dhabi, about $30m (groundbreaking Oct 2025).
Source: Gulf News, https://gulfnews.com/business/corporate-news/nanjing-kenyo-group-launches-middle-easts-largest-3d-printing-factory-in-abu-dhabi-1.500296159
Dubai Municipality's challenge to build a villa entirely with robots, with Zacua Ventures, Wurth and 25+ companies and universities. Still described as planned.
Source: Dubai Municipality, https://www.dm.gov.ae/dubai-municipality-launches-global-robotic-villa-challenge/
Also: Buildroid AI's block-laying robot piloted by ALEC, and a Dubai Municipality LiDAR survey robot.

Qatar (1)
UCC Holding and Ashghal printing two 20,000 m² public schools in Doha on COBOD printers.
Source: UCC Holding, https://uccholding.com/media/read/worlds-largest-3d-printed-construction-project-commences

Caveats: we only count what has a primary source and a date, so this undercounts.

If you work on sites here: what robots have you actually seen in use, and which of these look like PR rather than practice?

posts.title: Dubai wants 100 buildings ready for indoor delivery robots by 2029. Would your building let them in?
posts.text:
Dubai Future Labs has signed eight delivery firms (talabat, Keeta, Deliveroo, Careem, Quiqup, EMX, Aramex and noon) to a programme where the courier hands your order to a robot at the building entrance, and the robot takes it up to your door. The target is 100 robot-ready buildings by 2029.
Source: Entrepreneur Middle East, https://mena.entrepreneur.com/business-news/dubai-future-foundation-targets-robotic-deliveries-in-100-buildings-by-2029

Questions for anyone living in a tower here, or in Riyadh, Doha or Cairo:
Would you want this in your building, or would you rather the courier came up?
What would building management worry about: lifts, security, lobbies?
Has anyone already had a delivery robot in their building?

(I run roboticsmena.com, where we track these programmes. No link needed, I'm just curious what residents think.)

posts.title: Sobha Hartland now has robot deliveries on the pavement and a drone service on the way. Anyone actually used them?
posts.text:
Since December 2025, Yango's delivery robots have been carrying noon Minutes orders around Sobha Hartland. You pick the robot option in the noon app, track it on the map and unlock it with your phone. By May 2026 there were 10 of them, and Yango said it wanted 100 across the UAE within a year.

Last week Keeta Drone said Sobha Hartland will be one of the first communities for its new M-Drone 4L, which hovers and lowers orders of up to 4.5 kg on a 15 m cable instead of landing. No start date yet.

If you live there: how long does a robot delivery actually take, do they get stuck, and would you use a drone drop? Trying to work out how well this works day to day versus the press releases.

(Disclosure: I run roboticsmena.com, which tracks robot deployments in the region.)

Source: Yango Group and noon, 9 Dec 2025, https://www.zawya.com/en/press-release/companies-news/yango-group-and-noon-announce-strategic-partnership-to-scale-autonomous-robot-delivery-across-the-gcc-uh6o73ja
Source: tbreak, May 2026, https://tbreak.com/yango-delivery-robots-dubai-scale-100/
Source: Keeta Drone, 18 Nov 2026, https://www.zawya.com/en/press-release/events-conferences/keeta-drone-unveils-its-latest-delivery-solutions-at-dubai-future-week-2348805
